rule: Regress a family one rung when a session is followed by a next-day flare
summary: The 24 h response is the core of the pain-monitoring model: symptoms should be back to baseline by the next morning, and if not, load is reduced (Thomee; Silbernagel 2007; Sprague 2021). Trials reduce load rather than prescribe a fixed regression, so one rung is a reasonable translation. 'Flare' is undefined in config; the LBP consensus defines it as a worsening lasting hours to weeks that impacts usual activity, so operationally tie it to next-morning stiffness/pain above pre-session level.

sources.note: Pilot RCT (patellar tendinopathy): Pain-Monitoring Model = pain <= 5/10 during/after activity and back to pre-activity level by next morning; feasible, high compliance
Silbernagel 2007 RCT (n=38, Achilles): continued running/jumping under a pain-monitoring model was no worse than 6 weeks of active rest
Delphi LBP flare definition: a worsening lasting hours to weeks, hard to tolerate, impacting usual activities
Self-reported LBP flare associated with ~2.8 NRS points higher pain, more interference and analgesic use (11,817 surveys)
